AH02.title: Worker submits an asset -> it enters the pending queue
AH02.notes: G partial and BLOCKED ON A FIXTURE, measured 2026-07-28: asset_nodes has 95 rows, ALL seeder-created (auth_uid NULL on every one), ALL status='approved', ZERO pending and ZERO rejected, and 0 rows authored by any worker or supervisor. rcm_strategies is 172 approved / 0 unapproved. So the submit -> review -> approve/reject -> restore workflow has no data in any state but the terminal one, which is exactly why the PDDA arc's F21 (a worker's Pending-assets tile always reads 0) was never diagnosed - there has never been a pending asset to see. The fixture, not the walker, is the binding constraint (LB13/LB17 again).

AHK1.name: A governance decision needs an IDENTITY, not a name
AHK1.notes: OPEN on measured evidence (2026-07-28 ground). asset_nodes carries submitted_by and approved_by as TEXT while 0 of 95 rows have auth_uid at all, and the table has 0 audit triggers. So an approval - the governance act the whole queue exists for - is attributed to a typed NAME, recorded nowhere the database can vouch for, and performed on rows nobody is provably the author of. Distinct from PMK3, which covered a COMPLETION's tamper-evidence: this is the DECISION itself, plus the forgeable-name half PMK3 never had to face because pm_completions has a real auth_uid.

AHK2.name: A number that sets inspection timing must be FALSIFIABLE
AHK2.notes: OPEN on measured evidence. Weibull beta/eta, the P-F interval and FMEA RPN each DECIDE WHEN A MACHINE IS NEXT OPENED UP - they do not report history, they set future action, so being wrong is physical rather than cosmetic. Ground measured 172 RCM strategies and 300 FMEA modes, all approved, computed by edge functions (weibull-fitter, pf-calculator) with no in-repo oracle found. Each needs a stated method, a REFUSAL path when the data cannot support the fit, and a checkable oracle. Distinct from PMK1: that was a metric flattering what was DONE; this is a computed value deciding what happens NEXT.
